papers.title: Frobenius and perfection in framed motives
papers.abstract: We develop explicit Frobenius and perfection arguments for framed motives over imperfect fields. In positive characteristic, power framing homotopies and local framed transfers make relative Frobenius invertible after inverting the characteristic. Descent through successive Frobenius twists then gives a proof of strict homotopy invariance for homotopy invariant quasi-stable additive framed presheaves and identifies the canonical comparison with the perfect closure as a stable Nisnevich local equivalence of framed motives. We extend the comparison to E-framed motives for every motivic Thom spectrum E. It also yields the cancellation theorem and the cone theorem. For commutative symmetric Thom ring spectra, we identify triangulated categories of effective E-framed motives and effective E-modules and prove perfection invariance of these triangulated categories. All comparisons are made after inverting the exponential characteristic.

papers.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
papers.abstract: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$ are $3$-dualizable and non-degenerate but neither factorizable nor cofactorizable. This category is closely related to the line operators of linear Rozansky--Witten theory. Finally, we define an anomaly of a group action on an invertible braided monoidal $\infty$-category as a Witt class over $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, and show that the category of representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity is invertible relative to its quantum Frobenius.

papers.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
papers.abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.

papers.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.title: Stability theorems for $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets
papers.abstract:
We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $\eta$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $\eta\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $\eta$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $\eta\varepsilon$-fibrant.
  Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.

papers.title: $A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure
papers.abstract: Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$. At level $2$, we give explicit bracketing rules which make grounded partitions into affine crystal graphs of highest weights $2\Lambda_0$, $\Lambda_0+\Lambda_1$, and $2\Lambda_1$. We prove this by constructing explicit graph isomorphisms with the asymptotic model of Ariki and Mathas, whose vertices are Kleshchev multipartitions arising from Ariki-Koike algebras. Finally, we erase the $0$-arrows, which leaves the crystal graphs of the restrictions to the Levi subalgebra, and decompose them into finite strings. This decomposition gives new $q$-series identities at levels $1$ and $2$.

papers.title: A Central-Commutator Regge Seed: BCC Sublattices, Face-Matched Hinges, and Quaternionic Spectral Gaps
papers.abstract: (i) At the arithmetic parameter \delta = 1/3, the three short face diagonals of the negative-cycle ternary Gram form become mutually orthogonal and generate a simple-cubic sublattice of index two; the full lattice is body-centered cubic. (ii) The positive- and negative-cycle Gram tetrahedra admit matching hinge faces. A four-tetrahedron Regge star consisting of one negative-cycle tetrahedron and three positive-cycle tetrahedra has an exactly computable positive deficit angle. (iii) A figure-eight graph with quaternionic cycle holonomies i and j has a nonzero spectral gap; its characteristic polynomial is computed exactly and its smallest eigenvalue is isolated by rational bounds. (iv) The commutator [i, j] = -1 identifies the graph's central Z_2 obstruction with the negative signed-cycle class of the Gram construction. The statements are finite-dimensional results about lattices, piecewise-Euclidean complexes, and unitary graph connections. They do not construct a closed shell, a Lorentzian spacetime, or a solution of the Einstein-matter equations; they do not prove the dominant energy condition or dynamical stability. The term "negative-cycle" refers only to a sign invariant and has no implication of negative physical energy.

papers.title: A certified upper bound for the beat the average game
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be the supremum of $\mathbb{P}[X_1+X_2+X_3<2X_4]$ over all probability measures on $[0,\infty)$, where $X_1,\dots,X_4$ are independent with the given law. Determining $C$ is Problem 6.39, the beat the average game, in the list of Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner. Bellec and Fritz proved $0.4006953\le C\le 673/1615$ and conjectured that the lower bound, $0.4006953723\ldots$, is the exact value. We prove $C\le0.40069634$, less than $10^{-6}$ above the conjectured value. The proof applies Razborov's flag algebra method to samples of nine points. Since the points are independent, the positivity constraints of flag algebras hold for every single measure, so that no limit objects are needed. An exact certificate is checked in rational arithmetic, and the bound is also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with Lean's kernel checking the certificate.

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Realizability Conjecture for Surface Classes
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to Huang–Huh–Michałek–Wang–Wang’s conjecture on the real realizability of universally pseudoeffective surface classes.

papers.title: A Helly theorem for the Bruhat-Tits building
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a discretely valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}$. We show that a finite family of $\mathcal{O}$-lattices in $K^m$ is adapted to a common basis if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ $\mathcal{O}$-lattices is. In other words, in the Bruhat-Tits building of $\operatorname{GL}(m)$, a finite family of simplices lies in a common apartment if and only if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ simplices does. The proof uses a version of Radon's theorem for $\mathcal{O}$-lattices. We also give an alternative proof using truncated modules.

papers.title: A lower bound for Moser's worm problem with rotations and translations
papers.abstract: In its convex form, Moser's worm problem asks for the least area of a convex set in the plane that contains a copy of every arc of length $1$. For the version in which the copies may be rotated and translated but not reflected, we prove that this least area $M^{+}$ satisfies $M^{+}\ge0.2414$; the best bound before, $0.239$, follows from Keller's bound for the version with reflections. The proof bounds the area of the convex hull of copies of five polygonal arcs, among them two zigzags that turn in opposite directions, so that without reflections the hull must contain a zigzag turning each way. A branch and bound over the placements of the arcs, with second-order Taylor bounds for signed areas of polygons, produces a certificate, which is checked in ball arithmetic and in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: A lower bound for the Bohr radius of the bidisc
papers.abstract: We prove that the Bohr radius $K_2$ of the bidisc, whose exact value is unknown, satisfies $K_2>0.301665$, improving Patel's bound $K_2>0.30158758$. As in his argument, we pass to functions with positive real part and value $1$ at the origin; we bound the sum of the moduli of their coefficients of degree $n$ by $2S_n$ instead of $2\sqrt n$, where $S_n$ is the Sidon constant of $\{0,1,\dots,n\}$, and we bound $S_5$, $S_6$ and $S_7$ with computer-assisted certificates. In Lean 4 we also prove $K_2\ge0.301665$, assuming Patel's inequality coupling the coefficients of degrees two and three.

papers.title: A lower bound for the essential minimum of the Zhang–Zagier height
papers.abstract: For an algebraic number $\alpha$ let $h(\alpha)$ be its absolute logarithmic Weil height, and let $h_Z(\alpha)=h(\alpha)+h(1-\alpha)$. The essential minimum of $h_Z$ is the supremum of the numbers $H$ for which only finitely many algebraic numbers satisfy $h_Z(\alpha)\le H$. Zagier showed that it is at least $\frac12\log\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}=0.2406059\ldots$, and the best lower bound so far is $0.24874$, due to Flammang. We prove that the essential minimum is at least $0.24982933$. The proof combines Smyth's method of auxiliary functions, here with five integer polynomials in $z(1-z)$, with a logarithmic energy term relative to a measure on the circles $|z|=1$ and $|1-z|=1$. Resultants and discriminants of minimal polynomials are nonzero integers. They bound the polynomial terms and the energy term, and a condition on the degrees absorbs the leading coefficients, so the argument applies to all algebraic numbers. A superharmonicity argument reduces the positivity of the auxiliary function to the unit circle, where two separately written programs verify it in ball arithmetic for a certificate with exact rational data. We also prove this lower bound in Lean.

papers.title: A lower bound for the smallest limit point of the absolute Mahler measure of totally positive algebraic integers
papers.abstract: Let $\ell_+$ be the smallest limit point of the absolute Mahler measures $\Omega(\alpha)=M(\alpha)^{1/\deg\alpha}$ of totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha$. By work of Smyth, $\ell_+\le1.7274$, and the best lower bound was Flammang's $\ell_+\ge1.722069$. We prove that all but finitely many totally positive algebraic numbers $\alpha$ satisfy $\Omega(\alpha)>1.7234615$, and that $\ell_+>1.7234615$. We also prove that all but finitely many totally real algebraic numbers $\beta$ have absolute logarithmic Weil height $\log\Omega(\beta)>0.2721673$. The proof adds to Smyth's method of auxiliary functions the logarithmic energy term that Orloski, Talebizadeh Sardari and Smith derived from the integrality of discriminants for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem. The resulting inequality is verified rigorously by computer, and the lower bounds are also proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: A midpoint locally uniformly rotund Banach space with the Daugavet property
papers.abstract: We construct a separable Banach space with the Daugavet and Schur properties whose norm is midpoint locally uniformly rotund and G\^ateaux smooth. The construction combines the ergodic orbit norm of Dantas, Kaasik and Perreau with a Bourgain--Rosenthal enlargement in the form developed by Kadets and Werner.

papers.title: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
papers.abstract:
We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $\Delta_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $\Sigma_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology. Motivic conjectures relating algebraic cycles to special values of $L$-functions suggest that $\mathsf{Q}$ is nonzero in Chow. More precisely, we prove that the Chow nonvanishing of $\mathsf{Q}$ follows from a conjecture of Harder concerning the failure of the Manin--Drinfeld principle in genus 2.
  We prove that $\mathsf{Q}$ vanishes in cohomology by pairing with generators of the tautological ring. To prove $\mathsf{Q}$ is not in the set of $3$-spin relations requires an argument involving the $\Sigma_{14}$-representation-theoretic properties of the $3$-spin relations and the cohomology of local systems on $\mathcal{A}_2$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$. Parallel constructions for other moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n}$ are discussed in the paper. There are many open questions.

papers.title: A proof of the HLRV conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Hausel–Letellier–Rodriguez-Villegas conjecture on the mixed Hodge polynomials of generic semisimple \(\mathrm{GL}_n\) character varieties.

papers.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
papers.abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.

papers.title: A rational model for the fiberwise THH transfer I: Sullivan algebras
papers.abstract: Given a map $f$ of fibrations over a space $B$ such that the fiber of $f$ is simply connected and finitely dominated, we prove that its fiberwise THH transfer, considered as a map of parametrized spectra over $B$, is rationally modeled by the Hochschild homology transfer of a Sullivan model of $f$. The proof goes in two steps. Firstly, we use the machinery of higher categorical traces to show that the fiberwise THH transfer can be computed internally to parametrized spectra. Secondly, we model the resulting description rationally using work of Braunack-Mayer, who proved that parametrized spectra can be modeled by modules over Sullivan algebras. In Part II, we will use our result to obtain a rational model of the Becker-Gottlieb transfer, and for applications to manifold topology.

papers.title: Admissible Yang--Baxter equation for Nijenhuis perm superalgebras
papers.abstract: We develop a superization of the theory of admissible Yang--Baxter equations for Nijenhuis perm algebras initiated by Ma and Song. We introduce Nijenhuis perm superalgebras, their representations, and the dual representation, with Koszul signs chosen so that the contraction of the Yang--Baxter tensor matches the $\mathcal O$-operator equation exactly. We define Nijenhuis perm superbialgebras and characterise them by matched pairs. In the coboundary case, we show that every even supersymmetric solution of the $S$-admissible perm Yang--Baxter equation gives rise to a Nijenhuis perm superbialgebra, and we give sufficient conditions for a perm superalgebra to admit a Nijenhuis operator constructed from such a solution. Examples with purely odd components illustrate the role of the grading.

papers.title: Aigner's Three Monotonicities from Fibonacci Matrices and Six Snake Pieces
papers.abstract: Starting from the established fact that Markov numbers count perfect matchings of their Markov snake graphs, we give a self-contained proof of the fixed-sum, fixed-numerator, and fixed-denominator orderings proposed by Aigner. The author's Fibonacci-matrix normalization begins with $(AC)_{11}-(B^2)_{11}=2$ for consecutive odd-indexed Fibonacci blocks. Fibonacci matrices prove normalization and fixed-numerator monotonicity. The author's six-piece decomposition proves the remaining fixed-sum comparison and fixed-denominator monotonicity. We credit the matching correspondence to its original 2002–2003 REACH development and distinguish that history from the later ordering theorems.

papers.title: Algebraically independent counterexamples with rational-power separation
papers.abstract: Starting from Apicella’s private-prime construction, we give a proof draft of divergent reciprocal-logarithmic-weight examples that are algebraically independent, admit any prescribed positive integer-anchor error and have growing mixed-power gaps for rational dilations with bounded denominators. The integer numerator remains unrestricted. We record transcendence and field consequences and retain an elementary reconstruction of Apicella’s rational example in an appendix, with its prior-work attribution explicit.

papers.title: An edge comparison with constant 3/2 and the coefficient 6/sqrt(2 pi) for the average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
papers.abstract: For every real polynomial threshold function f of degree at most d on the uniform cube {-1,1}^n we prove AS(f) <= min{n, 6 d b_n (n+d)/(n+2d)} <= (6/sqrt(2 pi)) d sqrt(n) < 2.394 d sqrt(n), where b_n = E|B_n - n/2| for B_n ~ Bin(n,1/2). The previous coefficient was 8/sqrt(2 pi) = 3.1915... The new ingredient is an edge comparison with constant 3/2 in place of 2 in OpenAI's weighted-grading argument: for every positive weight and every sign function h, the number of ordered equal-sign edges of h is at most (3/2)||MH+HM||_HS^2. The proof rests on the exact identity (Z_i M Z_i - M)^2 = I - A_i^2, where A_i is the grade-diagonal part of the multiplication by x_i. Combined with OpenAI's original coupling estimate alone, the lemma already gives AS(f) <= 6 d sqrt(n).

papers.title: An Equivariant Landweber Exact Functor Theorem for Abelian Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract:
We prove an equivariant Landweber exact functor theorem for abelian compact Lie groups $G$. For a graded module $N$ over the $G$-equivariant Lazard ring $L_G$, we give necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $N$ for the functor
  \[
  X\longmapsto (MU_G)_*(X)\otimes_{L_G} N
  \]
  to define a homology theory on the category $\mathrm{Sp}^G$ of genuine $G$-spectra. Our criterion is obtained by varifying the Landweber exactness on each stratum indexed by a closed subgroup of $G$ and then gluing the local flatness data via Euler classes. As an application, we show that for any non-equivariant Landweber exact ring spectrum $E$, $MU_G\wedge_{MU} E$ is equivariantly Landweber exact, thereby proving a conjecture of Wisdom. Finally, we study the $G$-equivariant formal groups $\widehat E_G$ over $\hom(G^*,E)$ associated to elliptic curves $E/S$. We prove that its classifying map $\hom(G^*,E)\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{FG}}^G$ is flat whenever $S\to\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ell}}$ is flat, and recover $\widehat E_G$ from Gepner-Meier's equivariant elliptic cohomology associated to any oriented spectral lifting of $E/S$.

papers.title: An explicit bound below 2/π for the maximum term of an entire function
papers.abstract: For a transcendental entire function $f$ let $\mu(r)$ be its maximum term and $M(r)$ its maximum modulus on $|z|=r$. Erdős asked for the largest possible value $B$ of $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\mu(r)/M(r)$. An argument of Clunie gives $B\le 2/\pi=0.636619\ldots$, and Clunie and Hayman proved $B\le 2/\pi-c$ for an absolute constant $c>0$ that they did not compute. We prove $B\le0.63005$. We make the stability argument of Clunie and Hayman quantitative by testing $f$ against trigonometric polynomials at one or both of two consecutive radii where the central index jumps. The proof is computer-assisted, and the theorem is also proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: An explicit determinantal formula for Sinkhorn limits of matrices and tensors
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula, as a single determinant, for the polynomial satisfied by any entry of the limit obtained by scaling a positive tensor of format $n_1\times\dots\times n_r$ to arbitrary prescribed one-dimensional margins (Sinkhorn--Knopp scaling, Kruithof's method, iterative proportional fitting). The polynomial is the multilinear resultant, on the Segre variety $\PP^{n_1-1}\times\dots\times\PP^{n_r-1}$, of the linear forms expressing the margin conditions. Its degree is the multinomial coefficient $N=\binom{d}{n_1-1,\dots,n_r-1}$ with $d=\sum_k(n_k-1)$, and for generic tensors its roots are the corresponding entries of all complex solutions of the scaling equations. A Sylvester matrix turns it into an explicit $N\times N$ generalized eigenvalue problem, whose null vector recovers the whole limit. The leading coefficient is the principal $A$-determinant of the product of simplices, that is, the product of the hyperdeterminants of all faces of the tensor. The constant term is likewise a product of face hyperdeterminants, and the faces avoiding the chosen entry split off as a factor independent of that entry. For matrices we also give a short proof, in Pl\"ucker coordinates, of a diagonal form of the eliminant. For every positive tensor, the limit is the unique root for which the Sylvester matrix has a positive null vector of monomials. Generically, the other roots are the corner entries of the solutions of the same scaling equations with complex scaling factors.

papers.title: An Irredundant Test for Circular Positivity
papers.abstract: We give an inclusion-minimal circular-minor positivity test on five boundary vertices that is not weakly separated. This refutes the inclusion-minimal version of Conjecture 6.3.4 of Alman, Lian and Tran.

papers.title: An unconditional estimate and the structure of the Bäcklund orbit
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be an arbitrary $C^\infty$ solution of the sine-Gordon equation $f_{xy}=\sin f$ in the square $W=[-L,L]^2$, and let $\omega_n$ be obtained by $n$ successive B\"acklund transformations with arbitrary real parameters $a_1,\dots,a_n>0$ and arbitrary normalization constants $c_j$. For a solution $\omega$ let $r(\omega)$ be the associated smooth map of a surface of curvature $K=-1$ (Chebyshev net, common initial frame at the origin). We prove the unconditional estimate $\|r(\omega_n)-r((-1)^n f)\|_{L^\infty(W)}\le K_n\sum_{j=1}^n 1/a_j$, $K_n=3L^2+(1+L)\pi(2T_*+\pi)3^{n-1}$, $T_*=\sup_{|x|\le L}\int_{-L}^{L}|f_y|\,dy$, with no restrictions on the $a_j$, their ratios, the $c_j$, or $L$. The proof reduces the problem to a cascade of forced pendulum equations, controlled by an integral Lyapunov estimate and by cumulative estimates for the orthogonal Gauss-Weingarten propagator. For the Amsler seed $f=Y(xy)$ we show $T_*\le 2L^2$, which gives an explicit constant; the order $1/a$ is sharp. We also study the dependence on the data: smoothness along finite-dimensional families, continuity on the Fr\'echet data space, convergence of the immersions in $C^0$ and $W^{1,p}$ although the solutions $\omega_n$ themselves need not converge, partial limits along arbitrary index sets for $a_j\to\infty$ and for $a_j\to0$, and a two-chamber structure of the orbit under B\"acklund chains.

papers.title: An upper bound for the connective constant of the square lattice
papers.abstract: We prove that the connective constant $\mu$ of the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, the exponential growth rate of the number of $n$-step self-avoiding walks, satisfies $\mu\le2.6586513$. The previous best upper bound, $\mu\le2.662342426$, is due to Couronné. Like the bounds of Pönitz and Tittmann and of Couronné, ours comes from a finite automaton that remembers a bounded part of the past of the walk. The new idea is to count bridges. Since they can all be preceded by the same infinite history, the automaton may treat as visited the unvisited cells that no infinite self-avoiding continuation can reach, and three tests on the current state and the next step recognize such cells. The bound is checked in exact integer arithmetic and proved in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: An upper bound for the smallest limit point of the absolute Mahler measure of totally positive algebraic integers
papers.abstract: Let $\ell_+$ be the smallest limit point of the values of the absolute Mahler measure $\Omega(\alpha)=M(\alpha)^{1/\deg\alpha}$ on totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha$. Smyth's work gives $\ell_+\le\ell^2=1.72731\ldots$, where $\ell=1.31427\ldots$ is the limit point that he found for totally real algebraic integers. We prove $\ell_+\le1.7239501$, and that infinitely many totally positive algebraic integers satisfy $\Omega(\alpha)<1.7239501$. Together with the lower bound $\ell_+>1.7234615$ of a companion paper, this places $\ell_+$ in an interval of length less than $4.9\cdot10^{-4}$. The proof exhibits a measure $\mu$ on $[0,9]$ with a piecewise linear density on $3{,}481$ rational nodes. Its logarithmic potential is bounded below by a combination of $\log|Q|$ for $21$ irreducible polynomials $Q$, namely $x$ and polynomials taken from Flammang's work. By a criterion of Smith, $\mu$, normalized to mass $1$, is a limit of distributions of conjugates of totally positive algebraic integers, and its integral of $\log^{+} x$ gives the bound. Two separately written programs verify the conditions in ball arithmetic. Both results are also proved in the Lean proof assistant, assuming Smith's theorem and a lower bound for the potential of the arcsine measure, with the checks of the certificate run either as compiled code or by Lean's kernel.

papers.title: An upper bound of 2√2 for the three-dimensional sofa problem in a snake-shaped corridor
papers.abstract: The moving sofa problem in a snake-shaped corridor, posed by O'Rourke and by Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner, asks for the largest volume of a connected body that can be moved through a corridor of unit-square cross-section with two turns that are far apart, one in the $x$–$y$ plane and one in the $y$–$z$ plane. The largest reported body has volume at least $1.8558404$, and Tang obtained upper bounds for this problem, the best of which is $3.4083$. We prove by hand that the largest volume is at most $2\sqrt2$ whenever the straight section between the turns is longer than $2+\sqrt2$. The main new tool is a sharp bound: two infinite tubes of unit-square cross-section whose axes make an angle $\theta$ meet in volume at most $1/\sin\theta$. With it, Hammersley's argument for the planar moving sofa problem carries over to three dimensions. The same argument gives explicit bounds for shorter straight sections; these and the main bound have also been proved in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Automorphisms of the modular curves $X_\Delta(N)$
papers.abstract: We show that every automorphism of a modular curve $X_\Delta(N)$ of genus at least $2$, where $\Gamma_1(N)\subseteq \Gamma_\Delta(N)\subseteq \Gamma_0(N)$, is induced by the normalizer of $\Gamma_\Delta(N)$ in $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, except for five curves, namely $X_0(37)$, $X_0(63)$, $X_0(108)$, a curve of level $37$ found by Jeon, Kim and Schweizer, and a curve of level $63$ whose non-modular automorphisms had, to our knowledge, not been noticed before. In particular every automorphism of $X_1(N)$ normalizes the group of diamond operators, as claimed for square-free $N$ in an unpublished preprint of Momose. The proof combines a twisted Hecke relation, which comes from the Galois action on the Tate module of the Jacobian, with a uniform bound for the dimension of the CM part of the Jacobian and with computations for finitely many levels.

papers.title: Axiomatic Foundations of Astrophysical Systems: Model-Independent Obstructions Between Equations of State, Observables, and Field Equations
papers.abstract: Continuing the axiomatic program for astrophysics initiated in previous works, we introduce a gravity-model-independent and scale-independent definition of an \emph{astrophysical system} and of \emph{clusters of astrophysical systems} over arbitrary piecewise smooth spatial manifolds. A cluster is modeled as a subspace of piecewise differentiable sections of matter and gravitational bundles (modulo coincidence on dense open sets), endowed with macroscopic observable functionals and coupled through a parametric field operator $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{grav}}$ encompassing Newtonian gravity, General Relativity, and modified gravity theories ($f(R)$, Rastall, scalar-tensor, and MOND-type models). Restricting local equations of state to bounded extended-norm balls (which form affine Banach spaces on fixed partitions) and applying Implicit Function Theorems in locally convex spaces, we prove four universal obstruction theorems: (i) a direct multi-observable obstruction theorem; (ii) a gravity-coupled structural obstruction theorem via locally density-solvable field equations and reference evaluation operators; (iii) a causal lifting theorem for general acoustic cones; and (iv) an \emph{inverse obstruction theorem}, showing that combining causality-constrained equations of state with empirical observable relations induces \emph{a priori} bounds on the parameter space of the gravitational theory. We also prove that finite-dimensional gravity-coupled clusters are closed and nowhere dense in any Hausdorff locally convex topology, and apply our results to compact stars in Rastall and perturbative $f(R)$ gravity, Bowers--Liang anisotropic stars, and galaxies obeying the Baryonic Tully--Fisher Relation.

papers.title: Bounds for the sign uncertainty constant in dimension one
papers.abstract: Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane proved that a nonzero even real function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $f$ and $\widehat{f}$ integrable, $f(0)\le0$ and $\widehat{f}(0)\le0$ cannot have $f$ and $\widehat{f}$ both nonnegative outside an arbitrarily small neighborhood of the origin. The sharp constant in this sign uncertainty principle is $A_+(1)$, the infimum of $\sqrt{A(f)A(\widehat{f})}$ over all such $f$, where $A(f)$ is the radius beyond which $f$ is nonnegative; its square is the constant of Problem 6.11 in the list of Georgiev, Gómez-Serrano, Tao and Wagner. We prove $0.5502<A_+(1)\le0.5509$, improving the previous bounds $0.45\le A_+(1)\le\sqrt{0.3089}$; in particular $A_+(1)<0.555$, as conjectured by Gonçalves, Oliveira e Silva and Ramos. The lower bound comes from a weight in the spirit of the summation formulas of Cohn and Gonçalves, built from Gaussians and cosines and corrected near the origin by an approximate solution of a Fredholm integral equation, and the upper bound from an explicit self-dual combination of Gaussians. The numerical inequalities in both proofs are verified in ball arithmetic, and the bounds $0.5502\le A_+(1)\le0.5509$ also have formal proofs in Lean 4.

papers.title: Bounds for the smallest limit point of the areal Mahler measure of totally positive algebraic integers
papers.abstract: Pritsker's areal analog $\|P\|_0$ of the Mahler measure replaces the integral of $\log|P|$ over the unit circle by its integral over the unit disc with respect to normalized area. For an algebraic number $\alpha$ of degree $n$ with minimal polynomial $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$, taken primitive with positive leading coefficient, let $N_0(\alpha)=\|P\|_0^{1/n}$. Flammang proved that $N_0(\alpha)\ge1.380047$ for every totally positive algebraic integer $\alpha$ outside an explicit finite set. We prove that the smallest limit point of the values of $N_0$ on totally positive algebraic integers and their essential minimum lie between $1.3830134$ and $1.3839579$. The lower bound improves on Flammang's constant: it holds for all but finitely many totally positive algebraic numbers, not only integers, although the exceptions are not determined. Infinitely many totally positive algebraic integers satisfy $N_0(\alpha)<1.3839579$. The lower bound comes from an auxiliary function with a logarithmic energy term, and the upper bound from an explicit measure that, by a criterion and a theorem of Smith, is a limit of distributions of conjugates of totally positive algebraic integers. The inequalities behind both bounds are verified in ball arithmetic, and both bounds are also proved in Lean, the upper one assuming Smith's theorem.

papers.title: Bounds for the weak type (1,1) constant of the centred maximal operator over squares
papers.abstract: Let $c_2$ be the best constant in the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for the centred Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator over axis-parallel squares in the plane. We prove $1.7027237335\le c_2\le3.59123$, improving the bounds $1.6855\ldots\le c_2<3.615749$ obtained by Lin. The upper bound comes from a new kernel in Lin's comparison principle, which bounds $c_2$ by half the integral of a suitable kernel; closed forms for the fractional operator in this principle make its conditions checkable. The lower bound comes from a periodic measure obtained by modifying Lin's lattice of point masses. Both proofs are computer-assisted and formally verified in Lean.

papers.title: Certified upper bounds for the Chvátal–Sankoff constant
papers.abstract: Let $\gamma_2$ be the Chvátal–Sankoff constant, so that the expected length of a longest common subsequence of two independent uniformly random binary strings of length $n$ is $\gamma_2n+o(n)$. Lueker proved $\gamma_2\le0.826280$ with a finite automaton that reads a pair of strings as a sequence of minimal match pairs and remembers the last $h$ symbols of each string, for $h=8$. We carry out his method up to $h=13$ and prove $\gamma_2\le0.821963$. For $h=13$ the certificate lists $165{,}695{,}219{,}469$ states of the automaton, reduced by a symmetry. The bound rests on an explicit positive vector for the weighted transition matrix of the automaton; a checker rebuilds every transition with its own code and verifies the required inequalities in exact integer arithmetic. We also give a complete proof that the automaton accepts the truncated canonical decomposition of every pair of strings, the property on which the method depends. The bound $\gamma_2\le0.821963$ is also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with a computation evaluated by compiled code, and the bounds $\gamma_2\le0.825101$, $\gamma_2\le0.824120$, $\gamma_2\le0.823290$ and $\gamma_2\le0.822579$ for $h=9$, $10$, $11$ and $12$ by formal proofs that are checked entirely by the Lean kernel.

papers.title: Certified upper bounds for two sum-difference exponents
papers.abstract: For finite sets $A,B$ of real numbers and $G\subseteq A\times B$, Katz and Tao proved in 1999 that $\{a-b:(a,b)\in G\}$ has at most $N^{11/6}$ elements whenever $A$, $B$ and $\{a+b:(a,b)\in G\}$ have at most $N$ elements; by an argument of Bourgain, bounds of this kind give lower bounds for the dimension of Kakeya sets. We lower the exponent $11/6$ to $1.8273$, and to $1.8295$ in every abelian group. We also prove $|X-Y|\le|X+Y|^{1.4209}$ for all finite sets $X,Y$ of integers, improving the exponent $1.4543$ of Kleinwaks; through his transfer theorem, this lowers the upper bound for the sum-difference constant of Gyarmati, Hennecart and Ruzsa from $1.3124$ to $1.2962$. Both proofs add up entropy inequalities among integer combinations of coordinates of several copies of a random pair, with rational weights found by linear programming; all four bounds are also proved in Lean 4.

papers.title: Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities
papers.abstract: The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization. Following the approach of Mumford and Morrison, we establish quantitative estimates for linear systems and their contributions to Chow weights, without restrictions on the Picard number.

papers.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
papers.abstract: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.

papers.title: Colossally Abundant Numbers and Nicolas' Second Criterion
papers.abstract: Robin's criterion states that the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $\sigma(n) < e^{\gamma} n \log\log n$ for every $n > 5040$. Nicolas' second criterion, in the form given by Broughan, states that it holds if and only if $n/\varphi(n) < e^{\gamma} \log\log n + e^{\gamma}(2 + \tau)/\sqrt{\log n}$ for every $n \geq N_{120569}$, where $N_{k}$ is the $k$-th primorial and $\tau = 2 + \gamma - \log(4\pi)$; for $N_{k}$ this inequality reads $c(p_{k}) < E(p_{k})$. Let $N$ be a colossally abundant number, let $q = p_{k}$ be the largest prime not exceeding the number $\xi(N)$ associated with $N$ by Nicolas, and write $\Delta(N) = \log(\sigma(N)/N) - \gamma - \log\log\log N$. For $\log q \geq 31$ we prove unconditionally that $1.317/(\sqrt{q}\log^{2} q) \leq \Delta(N) - c(q) + E(q) + (2\sqrt{2} - 2 - \tau)/(\sqrt{q}\log q) \leq 3.973/(\sqrt{q}\log^{2} q)$. Consequently, the second inequality for $N_{k}$ implies $\Delta(N) < -0.654/(\sqrt{q}\log q)$. We also prove that the primorials are the extremal cases of the second inequality, and that if it holds for every $N_{k}$ with $e^{31} \leq p_{k} \leq X$, then Robin's inequality holds for every $n > 5040$ with $\log n \leq X(1 - \log^{-3} X) - \log X$. A computation over the primes up to $X = 100{,}000{,}008{,}765{,}439$ verifies this hypothesis, so Robin's inequality holds unconditionally for $5040 < n \leq 10^{10^{13.6377}}$. To the author's knowledge, this is the largest range for which Robin's inequality has been verified: it extends the range $5040 < n \leq 10^{10^{13.11485}}$ of Morrill and Platt.

papers.title: Complex central configurations of the planar five-body problem at special masses
papers.abstract: We study the complex solution sets of the polynomial system for planar central configurations of five bodies, modulo rotations, at the masses $(1,4,4,4,4)$, $(1,1,4,4,4)$ and $(9,36,36,36,4)$, where the proof of finiteness for all positive masses in a companion paper counts the real central configurations. At $(1,4,4,4,4)$ the solution set is the union of $36$ explicit, pairwise disjoint irreducible curves and a finite set; the curves contain the modified Roberts continuum of Albouy and Kaloshin, up to relabelling the bodies, but none of their points is a positive central configuration. At $(1,1,4,4,4)$ the solution set is finite, and at $(9,36,36,36,4)$ the potential, which is positive at every central configuration, vanishes identically on every curve in the solution set, so these curves contain no positive central configuration. Finiteness at these masses, their positive multiples and their permutations therefore follows without a count. We also show that at positive masses two of the limit diagrams of Albouy and Kaloshin occur only for masses on finitely many explicit curves in the projective space of masses.

papers.title: Constructions and explicit power savings for point--unit-circle incidences
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal U(n,m)$ be the maximum number of incidences between $n$ distinct points and $m$ distinct unit circles in the plane. We give two constructions and an explicit upper bound for this function. Writing $s=\min(n,m)$ and $M=\max(n,m)$, the first construction gives a four-piece monomial lower bound for all cardinalities, with balanced exponent $1.041169920$. The second gives balanced configurations along an unbounded sequence with exponent $1.0431722305539701$, and further unbalanced configurations. The upper bound is $\mathcal U(n,m)\ll M+s^{2/3-2\delta}M^{2/3+\delta}$, where $\delta=2^{-2^{664}}/514560000000>2^{-2^{665}}$. The constructions use two windows in a relative-norm-one number-field lattice, strengthened arithmetic estimates, and interpolation between local profiles. The upper bound uses finite incidence regularization, prediction, arithmetic heights, and a six-by-five rigidity obstruction. The resulting bounds for the unit-distance problem follow as corollaries.

papers.title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the spaces of \(\delta\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(\delta\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(\delta=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(\delta=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

papers.title: Density-One Uniqueness for Markoff–Hurwitz Solutions
papers.abstract: For each fixed integer $n\ge4$, we prove that almost every positive integer solution of $\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2=n\prod_{i=1}^n x_i$ is determined up to permutation by its largest coordinate. The density is taken over sorted solutions with largest coordinate at most $R$, as $R\to\infty$.

papers.title: Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers
papers.abstract: We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by \'etale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.

papers.title: Descent properties for an abelian variety with extended Galois representation
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field, $L$ a finite Galois extension of $K$, and $X$ an abelian variety defined over $L$. If $X$ is isogenous over $L$ to an abelian variety defined over $K$, then the $\ell$-adic Galois representations associated to $X$ extend to representations $\bar{\rho}_{\ell,X}:\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{L}/K)\to\mathrm{Aut}(V_\ell X)$ for every prime $\ell$. This paper aims to show that the converse is true for abelian varieties of Type I, with some supplementary conditions needed on the endomorphisms of $X$, when $L$ is either a number field or a function field of prime characteristic different from $2$.

papers.title: Dualizing involutions on Kazhdan-Patterson covers of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(r,F).$ Let $r,n \geq 2$ and $\widetilde{G}$ be an $n$-fold Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $G$. Let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth representation of $G$ and $\pi^{\vee}$ be the contragredient of $\pi$. Let $\tau$ be an involutive anti-automorphism of $G$ satisfying $\pi^{\tau}\simeq \pi^{\vee}$. In this case, we say that $\tau$ is a dualizing or duality involution. When $r=2$, it is known that any lift of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution if and only if $n=2$. In this paper, we study the dualizing property of the lifts of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ and prove the following: (i) When $r \geq 2$ and $n \geq 3$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is never a dualizing involution. (ii) When $r=2t$ and $n=2$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution. (iii) When $r=2t+1$ and $n=2$, we show that there is a unique lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ which is a dualizing involution.

papers.title: Eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices: Non-convexity and Geometry
papers.abstract: A real symmetric matrix is called $d$-locally positive semidefinite if all of its $d \times d$ principal submatrices are positive semidefinite. We investigate the spectral geometry of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices. The set of vectors of eigenvalues of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $n \times n$ is fully understood and known to be convex when $d \in \{1,n-1,n\}$ \cite{blekherman2022hyperbolic}. In the smallest remaining case $n=4, d=2$, non-convexity of the set of vectors of eigenvalues was proved in \cite{kozhasov2023eigenvalues}, but even in this case the full description was unknown. We provide a basic semialgebraic description of the set of vectors of eigenvalues for $n=4, d=2$ by establishing a Fischer-type inequality for $2$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $4 \times 4$. We prove non-convexity for all $n \geq 4$ and $2 \leq d \leq n - 2$. For $d=2$ we prove a natural linear inequality on a linear slice of eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices which is tight at exactly two points. This gives a stronger proof of non-convexity in this case. For $d \in \{2, n - 2\}$, analyzing this slice involves solving certain non-smooth and non-convex min-max point configuration problems in the complex plane, which could be of independent interest. Similar problems were considered in \cite{nesterenko2024submatrices,sengupta2026submatrices} in the context of matrix decomposition and approximation.

papers.title: Ekeland–Hofer capacities and convex duality: ordinary and real spectral invariants
papers.abstract: We identify the rational Ekeland–Hofer capacities of convex bodies with Clarke’s homogeneous dual-action selectors by a direct minimax argument. Convex reduction and a common nonresonant quadratic tail give the cohomological real analogue for bodies invariant under a linear anti-symplectic involution. In the real case, the mod-two index of half-period translation requires linking in the presence of fixed Fourier modes. The real selectors are full actions of generalized brake characteristics and converge to twice the least brake action. Convex approximation includes nonsmooth bodies, and Fourier decomposition computes both sequences on diagonal ellipsoids.

papers.title: Electric-field hotspot packing and power channels in dielectric media
papers.abstract: We study quantified versions of two questions on field concentration and power channels posed by Miller and Monticone in OQ14. At a fixed driving frequency and under a common positive permittivity bound, we construct arbitrarily many simultaneous localized electric-field peaks in a single driven field, both in a two-dimensional invariant setting and in finite three-dimensional dielectrics. We also construct arbitrarily many localized peaks in a single normalized outgoing mode of a finite smooth dielectric, with prescribed real part of the complex resonance frequency and an arbitrarily high quality-factor target. The modal normalization is a reciprocal-residue normalization. Its relation to other possible interpretations of the original modal-volume question requires separate justification. For a specified channel definition, we construct, for every finite $N$, an $N$-dimensional counted input space through the same square section at fixed frequency, material bounds, and thresholds. The construction applies when the permitted absolute-bypass threshold exceeds the required passage threshold and when the selected output is the complete outgoing scattering map, including reflection. Thus the corresponding unrestricted uniform finiteness assertion fails. The result does not decide stricter bypass conditions or receiving-only output formulations. These quantified results do not resolve every interpretation of the original OQ14. The formal verification and its scope are described in the manuscript.

papers.title: Equality cases and every-copy results for the Werner endpoint inequality
papers.abstract: Whether every entangled state with a non-positive partial transpose (NPT) can be distilled is open. For the Werner states $\rho(d,\alpha)$, a criterion of Costa Rico reduces $k$-copy undistillability to an inequality for matrices of rank at most two: an alternating sum of the squared norms of their partial traces must be nonnegative. At $\alpha=-1/2$ we call it the endpoint inequality. It is known for two and three copies, and if it held for every $k$ in some dimension $d\ge3$, NPT bound entanglement would exist. For two copies we show that every equality case has rank two, with its range and that of its adjoint in products of two-dimensional subspaces. We also show that a first failure would produce, at some $\alpha>-1/2$, an equality case whose range has reduced states of rank at least three on every copy, unlike all known equality cases at $\alpha=-1/2$. For every $k$ we prove the endpoint inequality on an explicit class of matrices whose ranges generically have such reduced states. For four copies we give a computer-assisted proof of it in every dimension for all matrices $C$ such that the ranges of $C$ and of its adjoint lie in one two-dimensional subspace, as they do for all normal matrices of rank two.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves
papers.abstract: For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices. These results are proved using tools from homogeneous dynamics, in particular, the key dynamical input is a recent adelic equidistribution theorem due to Einsiedler, Margulis, Mohammadi, and Venkatesh.

papers.title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region and the fixed lift is integral, we prove that, at every positive regular integral level $d$, the space of sections on the cut is the sum of the fibre-rotation weight spaces of weight at most $d$ in the original quantisation. The higher cohomology of the cut pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes, so its equivariant index is the character of its actual section space. Using the moment polyptychs introduced in a companion paper (arXiv:2610.37724), we give an orbifold Kawasaki-Riemann-Roch localisation formula for this character. We also compute it as a weighted lattice-point sum: a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if the arrangement slack function satisfies $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. The examples compare these calculations in rank one, including a cut with an orbifold point, and in rank two, for smooth cuts that are not toric.

papers.title: Equivariant resolution of singularities for $T$-varieties in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let the ground field be algebraically closed of positive characteristic. We prove that every variety endowed with an algebraic torus action whose general orbits have codimension at most three admits an equivariant resolution of singularities. The proof combines the description of such varieties in terms of proper polyhedral divisors and divisorial fans, the existence of log resolutions in dimension at most three, and the resolution of toroidal embeddings established by Kempf, Knudsen, Mumford and Saint-Donat.

papers.title: Essential enhancements of site percolation in every dimension and on periodic lattices
papers.abstract: We prove Conjecture 1 of Balister, Bollobás and Riordan for site percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$ in every dimension $d\ge2$: for every essential enhancement, activated at any positive density, the enhanced configuration percolates for all $p<p_c$ close enough to the critical probability $p_c$. Aizenman and Grimmett gave an argument for this in 1991, but Balister, Bollobás and Riordan found that its combinatorial step can fail. They proved the cases $d=2,3$, outlined proofs for bond percolation on $\mathbb Z^d$ and for site percolation on the triangular lattice, and left the cases $d\ge4$ open. Near a site that is pivotal for a long connection, our proof reroutes the open path through a finite configuration in which the enhancement creates a connection, inside a ball that need not be centred at the pivotal site. A theorem valid in every dimension makes this possible unless the first and last sites of the path in the ball lie at a corner of the ball, and a mass-transport argument finds a ball where they do not. The method extends to site percolation on fourteen further periodic lattices, among them all Archimedean lattices other than the square lattice, and to bond percolation on the honeycomb lattice. The proof for $\mathbb Z^d$ uses no computer, parts of most lattice proofs are finite computer checks of local configurations, and the main theorems for $\mathbb Z^d$ and for nine of the lattices have been checked in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Evaluating the Generalizability and Explainability of Firn Image Classification with Topological Features
papers.abstract: In this paper we evaluate the performance of topological features for generalizable and explainable classification of firn image data, with the broader goal of understanding the advantages, pitfalls, and trade-offs in topological featurization. Firn refers to layers of granular snow within glaciers that haven't yet been compressed into ice. This compaction process imposes distinct topological and geometric structure on firn that varies with depth within the firn column. However, the limited and highly correlated training data available results in naive classifiers (such as convolutional neural networks) overfitting to orientation-dependent features. This motivates us to evaluate topological data analysis (TDA) as a way to design features which capture the shape of the firn data while retaining a large degree of invariance. We evaluate two classes of topological features, sublevel set features and distance transform features, together with persistence curves, to predict sample depth from firn images. A range of challenging training-test scenarios reveals that no one choice of method dominates in all categories. In particular, we see a tradeoff between accuracy on the one hand, and generalizability and explainability (via feature importance) on the other.

papers.title: Exact module categories over $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of indecomposable exact module categories over the finite tensor category $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$ of representations of the small quantum group $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, where $q$ is a root of unity of odd order. Each of them is given as the category of representations of a left comodule algebra over $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ explicitly presented by generators and relations.

papers.title: Exceptional model structures and the induced extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: A Hovey triple $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{W})$ is {\it exceptional}, if $(\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F} \cap \mathcal{W})$ is not a Frobenius pair. One has a disjoint union $\{\text{Hovey triple}\} = \{\text{Hereditary Hovey triple}\} \ \dot\bigcup \ \{\text{Exceptional Hovey triple}\}$ \ $\dot\bigcup \ \{\text{non-hereditary and non-exceptional Hovey triple}\}.$ Exceptional Hovey triples appear widely. For a selfinjective Nakayama algebra $A= kC_n/J^t$, $A\mbox{-}{\rm mod}$ admits exceptional Hovey triples if and only if $\gcd (n, t) \ge 2$ and $t \geq 3$. Their homotopy categories reveal new phenomena. Nakaoka-Palu's Theorem implies that there is a triangulation on $\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}.$ It is proved that a Hovey triple in a weakly idempotent complete extriangulated category $(\mathcal A, \mathbb E, \mathfrak s)$ is exceptional if and only if the induced extriangulated structure $\bigl(\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}, \ \overline{\mathbb E}, \ \overline{\mathfrak s}\bigr)$ is not {\it canonically triangulated}. Between this extriangulated structure and the one arising from the triangulation, the intermediate extriangulated structures are in one-to-one correspondence with Serre subcategories of $\mathrm{fp}((\frac{\mathcal P(\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F)}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Ab})$.

papers.title: Exceptional sequences of line bundles on $\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_\ell=\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)\subset\mathbb{P}^\ell\times(\mathbb{P}^\ell)^\vee$ be the incidence variety of points and hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^\ell$. We prove that for every $\ell\ge 3$, every exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ of maximal length $\ell(\ell+1)=\operatorname{rk} K_0(X_\ell)$ is full. Together with the case $\ell=2$, due to Altmann, Hochenegger and Witt, this shows that for all $\ell\ge2$ an exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ is full if and only if it has maximal length. The proof translates exceptionality into a combinatorial condition on lattice points of $\operatorname{Pic}(X_\ell)\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$ and reduces fullness to sequences containing a non-orthogonal descent. A capacity count for admissibly ordered subsets rules out all but one family of descents; for that family we classify the possible configurations and verify generation using Euler sequences and Koszul complexes.

papers.title: Fano-Enriques threefolds of Fano index $>1$
papers.abstract: We study $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds of Fano index greater than $1$ whose Weil divisor class group has nontrivial torsion. We give a complete list of their possible numerical types: there are $176$ of them, which refine to $182$ possible graded Hilbert series. At least $40$ numerical types are realised: $27$ by quotients of weighted complete intersections by cyclic groups, twelve by quotients of threefolds of codimension $4$ or $5$ and one by a quotient of the del Pezzo threefold of degree $5$. Seventy-two numerical types are shown not to occur. In particular the torsion subgroup need not have prime order, and the Weil and $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano indices can be $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$ or $(1,4)$.

papers.title: Finitary Cartesian closed varieties and semigroup actions
papers.abstract: We build on some ideas of Richard Garner. Let $M$ be a monoid and $B$ a Boolean algebra. A matched pair $[B|M]$ consists of $B$ and $M$ satisfying some axioms introduced by Garner. He then showed that every such matched pair determines a Boolean left restriction monoid $S = S[B|M]$. In this paper, we show that the data of a $[B|M]$-set, an action of a matched pair, may be encoded by means of what we call a factorizable Boolean supported action by $S$. This means that the category of $[B|M]$-sets is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of $S$. We deduce, as a result of Garner's work, that every non-degenerate finitary Cartesian closed variety is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of some Boolean left restriction monoid $S$.

papers.title: Flat linearity of uniform groups
papers.abstract: A uniform group is a quotient $\mathbb Z_K^{*M}\to\Gamma\to\mathbb Z_K^M$ on which $S_M$ acts by permuting the generators, and a flat representation is a representation $\pi:\Gamma\to U_K$ such that each $\pi(g_i)$ has the $K$-th roots of unity as eigenvalues. These are the quasi-flat matrix models of the group duals $\widehat{\Gamma}\subset S_{KM}^+$. We show that $\mathbb Z_K^{*M}$ is flat linear, in the sense that its flat representations separate points, and that for finite groups, flat linearity and stationarity reduce to exact covering problems. We use this to compute a census, and to prove results on the Heisenberg and metabelian groups.

papers.title: Folding of cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary symmetrizable Cartan data and arbitrary positive braids, we prove that the Laurent homomorphism identifying corresponding seed variables restricts to a surjective algebra homomorphism between the corresponding cluster algebras. We also extend the Kimura--Oya quantum twist automorphisms to arbitrary positive braids after localization at the frozen variables, and prove that their commutative specializations commute with the folding homomorphisms.

papers.title: From Four-Dimensional Wilson Lattice Gauge Theory to Quantum Yang--Mills Theory: Construction with Proofs from Certified Assumptions, and the Record of Its Independent Validation
papers.abstract: We present a complete formal paper compiling the Lean-verified construction of quantum Yang--Mills theory submitted on October 28, 2026, and independently validated by the Yang--Mills Shepherding Committee. Starting from the Wilson definition of lattice gauge theory on a four-dimensional torus, we give full proofs of every step that can be carried out from the definitions: the field-label algebra, the finite lattice theory, and---under an explicit, individually certified package of renormalization-group and analytic assumptions (RG1)--(RG5), (UV1), (PH1)--(PH3), (AN1), (Y1)--(Y4), (B1), (C1)---the fixed-volume ultraviolet limit, the subsequential infinite-volume limit, the phase decomposition with clustering and full support, the Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction satisfying the Wightman axioms, and the Yang--Mills identification: the stress tensor and its Ward identity, the trace anomaly with the verified constant $3\dim_{\mathbb{R}}\mathfrak{g}/\pi^{4}$, the exclusion of a precise class of free-field descriptions, the one-loop running coupling, and the operator product expansion. The independent validation (clean rebuild, Lean kernel replay, Comparator runs, the verification of the OS axioms against an independent axiom system, and the lattice-law, Ward-identity, common-scale, short-distance, and OPE adapters) is recorded in the second part. Two errata to the source validation document are corrected in the text. For the mass gap we prove two logical boundaries: an explicit OS model satisfies all sixteen registered inputs, with E4 clustering (equivalently, vacuum uniqueness) holding, yet its Hamiltonian has no spectral gap, and a mass gap is equivalent to a uniform exponential rate in the clustering axiom E4; the sixteen registered inputs therefore do not imply a mass gap. The gap problem is reduced to a single volume-uniform, label-uniform rate (MG); the cluster-expansion, spectral, rate and Wilson-loop routes, the random-mechanics criteria, the source-level adjudication, and the complete status are recorded in an appendix. A positive mass gap, uniqueness of the infinite-volume limit, uniqueness of the vacuum of the mixed theory, and order-by-order agreement of the OPE with perturbation theory are not proved, and the paper records precisely what is and is not proved at every step.

papers.title: Further cases of the inductive Alperin–McKay condition
papers.abstract: We prove the inductive Alperin–McKay condition at every prime for finite simple groups of types $A$, ${}^2A$, $B$, $C$, and $F_4$, and for those of type $D$ in characteristic two. We also prove the corresponding block condition for all unipotent blocks of natural groups of type $D$ on their prescribed central quotients.

papers.title: General linear groups in tangent categories
papers.abstract: General linear groups are well-studied Lie groups that encode the linear symmetries of a finitely-dimensional linear space. In differential geometry, they are an important ingredient of various constructions, including fibre bundles and the frame bundle of a principal bundle. They also appear in algebraic geometry as affine group schemes. Their Lie algebra, known as the general linear Lie algebra, is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of square matrices, whose Lie bracket is given by the commutator. Building on previous work on Lie groups, in this paper we introduce general linear group objects in the context of tangent categories. We define the general linear group of a differential object as a classifier of the Kleisli parametrized linear automorphisms of the differential object, a class of maps that generalize linear automorphisms in a suitable sense. We prove that such a group can be entirely constructed via a tangent triple equalizer and use this characterization to prove that the Lie algebra of general linear group objects is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of linear endomorphisms.

papers.title: Geometric Equivalence of the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: We study the complex rational extensions of two sequences, called SeqImpar and SeqPar, and the way their geometric images relate to the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. We prove that I(z) = 5 − 4/(z − 1) maps the critical line Re(z) = 1/2 to the circle |w − 9| = 4, and that, for w = I(ρ), rational inversion recovers exactly the coordinates Re(ρ) and γ = Im(ρ). We show that SeqPar induces a second rational curve and that its extension is injective in the half-plane Re(z) > 0. To distinguish points corresponding to zeta zeros from the other points on these curves, we use a Dirichlet series weighted by the convergence errors of the sequences and prove the correspondence between its poles and the nontrivial zeros. This yields a geometric criterion rigorously equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis: all relevant poles of the transformed function must lie on the indicated circle. We present formulas for extracting ordinates using residues and contour integrals, together with numerical checks involving the first five known zeros. The results constitute an exact reformulation of the hypothesis, not a proof of its truth or an independent algorithm for computing new zeros.

papers.title: Geometric Root Calculators: Radical supports of orders five and nine and real-degree enclosures in the Pandrosion rectangle
papers.abstract: We study ruler-and-compass iterations for the positive root $X^{1/p}$ that share one rectangle, one power stage and one readout, and differ only in a support line. Every support approximates the same target function $\kappa_*(t)=(t-1)/(t^{1/p}-1)$ of the residual $t$, and the contact order of the approximation fixes the order of the iteration. Besides the classical supports of orders one to four we treat three radical supports. A decentered arc gives a globally monotone fifth-order iteration. Two supports have local order exactly nine for every real $p>2$ and converge monotonically from every positive start: a support built from two successive mean proportionals, with error constant $7/648$ for cube roots, and a combination of the arithmetic mean, the geometric mean and one conic mean of $1$ and $t$, with error constant $23/20736$ for cube roots, drawn with three arcs. For integer $p\ge 3$ one step costs at most $10p+9$ elementary traces for the decentered arc, $10p+11$ for the three-mean support and $10p+59$ for the nested support; measured by the efficiency index, and under the stated counting conventions, the three-mean support is preferable for every $p\ge3$. We then separate what is a finite construction from what is only a scalar statement: the fast iterations are finite constructions for rational degrees, whereas for irrational $p$ a single step is not. For arbitrary real $p\neq 0$ a power-free subdivision with one final Padé readout encloses the root with relative width at most $z^5/256$ in at most $15n+63$ traces after $n$ subdivisions (for $X>1$, $p\ge 1$). Global convergence and the local orders with their constants, for the three radical supports and every real $p>2$, are checked in Lean, as are the degree, approximation and efficiency statements; the drawing inventories are written protocols.

papers.title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

papers.title: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.

papers.title: Growth criteria for reciprocal series with nonincreasing weights
papers.abstract: Fix nonincreasing positive integer weights $w_0,\ldots,w_{d-1}$ and define $c>1$ by $(c-1)^2\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}w_jc^j=w_0$. If the total weight is at least two, we prove irrationality of $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(a_n^{w_0}\cdots a_{n+d-1}^{w_{d-1}})$ whenever the positive integers $a_n$ are strictly increasing and $\limsup_{n\to\infty}(\log a_n)/c^n=\infty$. For every nonconstant nonincreasing weight profile, this lowers the sufficient base in the general criterion of Barreto, Kang, Kim, Kovač and Zhang (Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), e70457, Theorem 3), with the classical base-2 criterion included in the comparison. For weights $(3,2,1)$ the base becomes $\sqrt[3]{4}$; staircase weights $(d,d-1,\ldots,1)$ give $(d+1)^{1/d}$. Irregular growth is allowed. A more general form permits nondecreasing sequences and positive integer numerators under polynomial size bounds.

papers.title: Hodge Structures in Sextic Fourfolds Equipped with an Involution
papers.abstract: To each ternary sextic $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ whose associated plane curve is smooth, the Shioda construction attaches a smooth sextic fourfold $X \subset \mathbb{P}^5$ whose defining equation $f(X_0, X_1, X_2) - f(Y_0, Y_1, Y_2)$ is fixed under the involution $\iota : (X_0, X_1, X_2, Y_0, Y_1, Y_2) \mapsto i \cdot (Y_0, Y_1, Y_2, -X_0, -X_1, -X_2)$. The induced action $\iota^* : H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ fixes a Hodge substructure $H \subset H^4(X, \mathbb{Q})$ whose Hodge coniveau is 1. By the general Hodge conjecture, we expect that there should exist a divisor $Y \subset X$ for which $H \subset \ker\left( H^4(X, \mathbb{Q}) \to H^4(X \setminus Y, \mathbb{Q}) \right)$. We verify this prediction in case the Waring rank of $f(X_0, X_1, X_2)$ takes on its minimum possible value, partially answering a question of Voisin (J. Math. Sci. Univ. Tokyo '15).

papers.title: Holomorphic one-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds of Kodaira codimension one
papers.abstract: We give a bimeromorphic classification of compact K\"ahler manifolds of Kodaira codimension one that admit a holomorphic one form without zeros.

papers.title: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
papers.abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.

papers.title: Homological percolation in characteristic two: the Ising gauge case
papers.abstract: Duncan and Schweinhart proved that the $i$-dimensional plaquette random-cluster model with cluster weight $q$ on the $2i$-dimensional torus has a sharp homological percolation transition at the self-dual point, for coefficients in a field of characteristic other than $2$. Their proof needs the point group of the lattice to act irreducibly on the $i$-th homology of the torus. In characteristic $2$ it does not, and the most important case is excluded: $q = 2$ with $\mathrm{F}_2$ coefficients, which represents the $(i-1)$-form Ising lattice gauge theory. We prove the theorem for $q = 2^r$ with $r \ge 1$ and $\mathrm{F}_2$ coefficients. The representation-theoretic step is replaced by a transfer-matrix inequality, the classical positivity of the partition functions of 't Hooft's electric-flux sectors; read in the random-cluster representation, this inequality compares the probabilities of homological events. As a corollary, for the ferromagnetic $(i-1)$-form Ising gauge theory on the $2i$-dimensional torus (Wegner's model when $i = 2$), the free energy of every nontrivial 't Hooft twist tends to $0$ below the self-dual coupling and to infinity above it as the torus grows. For Bernoulli plaquette percolation ($q = 1$) the characteristic-$2$ case remains open for $i \ge 2$; we describe obstructions to proving it, and on the $4$-torus we prove a computer-assisted divisibility theorem for the classes of integral giant cycles just above $p = 1/2$.

papers.title: Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations
