papers.abstract: We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the K\"ahler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.

papers.title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

papers.title: Integer-power separation does not force rational-dilation separation
papers.abstract: We construct an algebraically independent set with divergent reciprocal-logarithmic weight, arbitrary prescribed proximity to selected integers and growing integer-power separation on tails. Nevertheless, every tail contains arbitrarily close rational-dilation pairs for each member of a dense family. The necessary integer-power finite-state lemmas and their proofs are included. This supplies a contrasting construction to the bounded-denominator rational-power example in the companion paper.

papers.title: Karlsson matrices and the kagome lattice
papers.abstract: For the subfactor associated to a generic Karlsson matrix of order 6, the first 18 fixed-space dimensions are the Catalan numbers. We obtain this from the quantum group of a Di\c t\u a limit. A first additional invariant tensor for a quantum $2$-transitive overgroup of this group would give a probability measure on closed walks on the kagome lattice with prescribed local distributions. At every even level a straight walk forces its return path and rules out such a measure. At odd levels a family of staircase tests and a 7-letter certificate at level 15 exclude further first occurrences. The least remaining level is 19. We also give an application to free wreath products and examine the second-order variation of the fixed spaces at special parameters.

papers.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

papers.title: Motivic Invariants of Automorphisms and the Plane Cremona Group
papers.abstract: Recent work of Campbell and Zakharevich studies the $K$-theory spectrum of varieties. In previous work, the second author constructs a derived version of the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic, giving a map out of this spectrum. We analyse the morphism that the derived $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic induces out of $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. We obtain an explicit description of this map, which encodes information about automorphisms of varieties. We use Hermitian $K$-theory to obtain a geometric description for part of this morphism in terms of Hodge cohomology. This allows us to obtain structural results about the group $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. As an application, we use the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant minimal model programme for surfaces to construct an arithmetic invariant of a large class of involutions in the plane Cremona group. We use this to construct two non-conjugate de Jonqui\`eres involutions with isomorphic positive genus fixed curves over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic not $2$ with at least 6 elements which admits a quadratic extension.

papers.title: New lower bounds for Romanoff's constant
papers.abstract: Romanoff proved in 1934 that the integers of the form $p+2^a$, with $p$ prime and $a\ge1$, have positive lower density $d$. We prove that $d\ge0.110825$ and, conditionally on an upper bound for prime pairs that Johnston and Trudgian derive from Lichtman's work on primes in arithmetic progressions, that $d\ge0.119178$; the best lower bound so far was $0.10788$. The proof refines the method of Elsholtz and Schlage-Puchta, which bounds the second moment of the number of representations in each residue class modulo a fixed integer. Both bounds are certified by computer and also proved in the Lean proof assistant, with the analytic inputs as hypotheses.

papers.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.

papers.title: On $\mathbb J$-strata with Parahoric Stabilizers in Affine Deligne-Lusztig Varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the $\mathbb J$-stratification of basic affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties for a minuscule cocharacter $\mu$. This stratification was introduced by Chen-Viehmann and has been expected to serve as an interesting tool for studying basic loci in Shimura varieties. We parametrize the $\mathbb J$-strata whose stabilizers in the Frobenius-twisted centralizer group are parahoric by constructing a natural bijection to combinatorial invariants called small cocharacters. We further prove that the cardinality of these sets is equal to that of a certain subset of the Weyl group orbit of $\mu$. A relationship with the weakly fully Hodge-Newton decomposability of Chen-Tong is also discussed.

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $\chi(1)_p$ of $\chi(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $\chi$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2\pi i/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $\chi_P$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $\chi_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: On intersections of function fields
papers.abstract: Let $X:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{R}$ and $Y:\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{T}$ be holomorphic maps between compact Riemann surfaces such that $X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cdot Y^*M(\mathcal{T})=M(\mathcal{E})$, where $M(\mathcal{S})$ denotes the field of meromorphic functions on a Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}$. We study the problem of determining when the degree $[M(\mathcal{E}):X^*M(\mathcal{R})\cap Y^*M(\mathcal{T})]$ is finite and attains the minimal possible value $\mathrm{deg}\,X\cdot\mathrm{deg}\,Y$. When $X$ is a Galois covering, we give a complete characterization in terms of factorizations of $Y$ into an equivariant map followed by a Galois covering. We also establish some results without the maximality condition, as well as general results on the functional equation $A\circ X=B\circ Y$ when one of the maps involved is a Galois covering.

papers.title: On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes

papers.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve. We use the theory of BPS Lie algebras, their $\chi$-independence property (proven by Kinjo-Koseki), the recent proof of the stack version of $P=C$ due to Picovschi and Davison's analytic neighborhood theorem to reduce the conjecture to a comparison problem between (the 'pure' part) of the BPS Lie algebra asociated to the stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve and the BPS Lie algebra of the stack of representations of the preprojective algebra of the quiver $S_g$. This last step is taken care of by a quiver analog of Markman's tautological generation theorem for the BPS Lie algebra of arbitrary quivers (this last result is also proven by Davison and Hennecart).

papers.title: Points from Processes: Vakarelov’s Dynamic Mereotopology and Whitehead’s Point-Free Program
papers.abstract: Whitehead held that neither points of space nor instants of time should be primitive: both ought to be definable from relations between material things. Region-based theories of space have largely carried out the spatial half of this program, but the temporal half has remained informal. This paper offers an expository and philosophical account of Dimiter Vakarelov’s dynamic mereotopology, developed in five papers between 2010 and 2016, which aims at a theory of space and time that is point-free in this double sense. We argue that the program is best read as a staged realization of Whitehead’s demand. Each stage enriches the primitive spatio-temporal relations between changing regions just enough to recover a further layer of temporal structure: first moments without order, then an ordered time, and finally nameable, spatially non-trivial epochs. The staging culminates in a structural result Whitehead anticipated but never formalized: points of space and points of time turn out to be different aggregations of one and the same stock of abstract atoms. We also argue that the representation theorems on which the program rests deliver a reconstruction, rather than a reduction, of points, and that reconstruction is what Whitehead’s program requires.

papers.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
papers.abstract: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.

papers.title: Positivity of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate various positivity properties of line bundles on general blow ups of Hirzebruch surfaces motivated by \cite{Han}, where the author has studied general blow ups of $\mathbb{P}^2$. For each of the properties: ampleness, global generation, very ampleness, and $k$-very ampleness, we provide several sufficient numerical conditions.

papers.title: Projective surfaces with infinite fundamental group and trivial profinite completion
papers.abstract: For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\) of odd order, we construct a smooth complex projective surface with infinite topological fundamental group and trivial \'{e}tale fundamental group. The isomorphism types of its finite subgroups are precisely those of the subgroups of \(A\). The surface is Kobayashi hyperbolic and has Stein universal cover.

papers.title: Random Abstract Cell Complexes
papers.abstract: In machine learning and signal processing, methods based on (abstract) cell complexes (CCs) are being applied successfully in different applications. However, there is currently a lack of random models, which are necessary for a thorough evaluation of these methods, both by generating synthetic data and as null models to compare results to. We fill this gap by defining a random model for abstract cell complexes based on independent inclusion probabilities, similar to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi model for graphs. We also discuss how modifications to bias the model to incorporate more structure can be implemented. The model can also be used to lift a graph (or other cell complex) to a cell complex of arbitrary dimension. The main challenge in this is that the number of cycles (possible 2-cells) on graphs is exponential, and the same is true in higher dimensions. We overcome this complexity with an approximate sampling algorithm limited to 2-cells (polygons) that is based on a recent advance in sampling cycles on a graph. Using this algorithm, we analyze the properties of random 2-dimensional CCs and showcase its usage as a performance baseline for both topological signal processing and topological deep learning. The algorithm is available in the package py-raccoon on the Python Package Index.

papers.title: Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion. For the variety of lines, we also prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation when $n\geq 8$, conditional on the finiteness of certain Tate-Shafarevich groups. For a smooth cubic hypersurface in $n$ variables, we prove that a line exists over the ground field when $n\geq 23$.

papers.title: Realizer Bounds and Repetition Constraints at the First Coefficient Crossing in the 3x + 1 Problem
papers.abstract: Terras’s coefficient stopping time conjecture asks whether the shortcut Collatz orbit of every integer n ≥ 2 lies below n when its coefficient ρk = 3d/2k first falls below one. Here k counts shortcut steps and d counts their odd inputs. We prove that every eligible realizer descends when the first-crossing word has at most 75 maximal runs of odd inputs. Any counterexample requires at least 76 such runs, 10 439 860 591 steps and 6 586 818 670 odd inputs. The proof uses a lower bound on the seed from the length of its odd runs, rational approximations to log2 3, the verified range of Rozier and Terracol, and Rhin’s estimate for a linear form in logarithms. We also prove descent for a family with arbitrarily many odd runs. Two further restrictions narrow the remaining words. An initial square U U in a failing word satisfies |U | < 35 log2 k. For a counterexample of shortest crossing length, the reciprocal-sum estimate of Nikzad, Frinkle and Bagherzadeh gives a lower bound on ρk whose value begins 0.9441733669 . . .. The open inequality compares the least eligible starting value in each remaining parity class with an explicit threshold.

papers.title: Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
papers.abstract: We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
papers.abstract: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gr\"obner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link is bounded above by the Hodge number $h^{2,1}$ of the base Calabi-Yau threefold. Both conjectures are proved here. The first holds for every polynomial with an isolated singularity, because its partial derivatives form a regular sequence; an independent derivation of the Sasakian Hodge numbers by sheaf cohomology on the leaf-space orbifold is also given. For the second, the stringy Hodge numbers of the Calabi-Yau orbifold are shown to bound the middle Sasakian Hodge numbers in every dimension $n\ge2$, and for $n\ge3$ the gap in $h^{n-1,1}$ is shown to be a sum of geometric genera of loci of orbifold points; for threefolds the bound is attained exactly when all curves of orbifold points are rational. The resulting closed formulae give the Sasakian Hodge numbers of the six $7$-dimensional links left open in the earlier work and complete datasets for all $95$ five-dimensional K3 links and all $1\,100\,055$ nine-dimensional Calabi-Yau fourfold links; for the K3 links they recover the previously known second Betti numbers.

papers.title: Schur Nonnegativity of Double-Wiring Cluster Variables
papers.abstract: We prove Cuenca’s conjecture that every cluster variable of the matrix cluster algebra associated with a double wiring diagram evaluates to a Schur nonnegative symmetric function on every generalized Jacobi–Trudi matrix. The result extends to cluster monomials.

papers.title: Self-embedding monoids and the existential Thomas conjecture
papers.abstract: We give a countable homogeneous finitely bounded Ramsey structure in a finite relational language with finitely many reducts up to first-order interdefinability but infinitely many self-embedding monoids of reducts. The reducts producing these monoids are first-order interdefinable, while their monoids form a strictly increasing chain. This refutes the existential strengthening of Thomas' conjecture even under the Ramsey hypothesis. The example is an ordered expansion of an equivalence-relation structure. Before the order is added, that structure has exactly five reducts up to first-order interdefinability. We also give a revised proof of the classification of self-embedding monoids for reducts of the countable existentially closed binary branching semilinear order. Exactly five monoids occur, refining its three-class first-order classification. The proof transfers the known classification for the homogeneous binary branching $C$-relation from antichains to arbitrary finite configurations. The additional step is a connectivity argument on finite labelled trees, using both preservation and reflection of the reduct's basic relations.

papers.title: Semiadditive Alternating Powers and Twisted Power Operations
papers.abstract: We study a class of representations of symmetric groups in higher semiadditive categories. For these representations in $\mathrm{Mod}^{\wedge}_{E_n}$, the transchromatic character of Hopkins--Kuhn--Ravenel and Stapleton is recovered as a sequence of monoidal characters on suitable categorifications, giving an explicit algorithm for its computation, and relating it to the iterated monoidal character in $(\infty,n)$-categories. These representations also give rise to notions of alternating powers and power operations in semiadditive categories, extending the classical alternating powers and $\lambda$-operations in $\mathrm{K}$-theory. We provide explicit computations in both the chromatic and higher categorical settings at low heights.

papers.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.

papers.title: SeqImpar and SeqPar: Analytic Characterizations of the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta and Dirichlet Beta Functions and a Criterion Equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: We study two rational sequences, called SeqImpar and SeqPar, originally defined by recurrences and converging to the common limit 5. The ratio of their convergence errors tends to 1/2. Using this ratio, we construct two Dirichlet series weighted by the von Mangoldt function and associated with the Riemann zeta function and the Dirichlet beta function. We prove that these series admit meromorphic continuations whose poles in the critical strip correspond exactly to the zeros of the respective functions, with residues equal to minus one-half of their multiplicities. We then prove that an estimate for the partial sum weighted by SeqImpar and SeqPar is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis, and state a parallel criterion for the Dirichlet beta function. The paper rigorously distinguishes proved identities, equivalences, and open problems: the coincidence of the number 1/2 with the critical line does not, by itself, constitute a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.

papers.title: Sharp Poisson approximation and second-order correction for long multiplicative runs
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be completely multiplicative with independent fair signs at primes. We count starts of constant runs of length at least $L$ in $[N,2N)$, with $L=\log_2N+O(1)$ and both signs included. The total variation distance to the Poisson law with nominal or exact mean has an explicit equivalent of order $LN^{-2/3}$, with a coefficient depending on $N2^{-L}$ and $L\bmod3$. After retaining the exact mean and second factorial cumulant, the quadratic Poisson–Charlier approximation has optimal error power $4/3$: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, its $\ell^1$ error lies between constant multiples of $N^{-4/3-\varepsilon}$ and $N^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$, uniformly in each fixed critical band. The leading correction comes from rational pairs. Keeping all channels up to a fixed height $h$ gives an explicit distance equivalent with power $h/(h+1)$, determined by the first omitted height. The third factorial cumulant has optimal power $41/30$. The proof expands around the exact Bernoulli marginals and stops at the first excluded dependent configuration. Arithmetic bounds for fixed configurations and a separate uniform tail estimate control the resulting positive boundary mass. Short square relations and a common algebraic curve bound the triple interactions; a fourth Charlier test detects the two-pair contribution that makes the quadratic exponent optimal.

papers.title: Smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and their automorphism groups
papers.abstract:
We consider smooth plane curves $\mathcal{X}$ of degree $d\geq4$, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, that possess a unique outer Galois point. This geometric condition forces the curve to be a cyclic covering of the projective line, and ensures that its automorphism group fits into a specific theoretical framework. For each possible non-cyclic reduced automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{red}}(\mathcal{X})$, we fully characterize the defining equation of $\mathcal{X}$ and the precise structure of its full automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{X})$.
  This comprehensive analysis not only identifies the exact form of the equation for each automorphism type but also establishes the detailed criteria under which these scenarios can occur, thereby offering a complete classification of defining equations for smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and a non-cyclic reduced automorphism group.

papers.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang--Baxter equation arising from posets
papers.abstract: We extend Victoria Lebed’s construction of idempotent solutions of the braid equation by introducing four families of solutions associated with posets. We show that every group can be realized as the automorphism group of such a solution, and establish a classification of solutions that either preserve or interchange the components of each pair. We also characterize when two solutions arising from posets are isomorphic. Finally, for finite posets, we construct two families of involutive solutions whose automorphism groups are explicitly described in terms of the automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of the underlying posets.

papers.title: Subrings and cotypes of truncated polynomial rings
papers.abstract: We study unital finite-index subrings of $R_n=\Z[t]/(t^n)$. We compute the cubic cotype function and the quartic total and cocyclic functions at every prime, including the exceptional factors at $2$, and prove the corresponding global counting theorems in degrees three, four, and five. Explicit Hermite sums with determinantal weights give full cotype formulas for $n=4,5$, without an asserted closed rational evaluation. We extend these calculations by a linear lifting recursion for every degree and by a two-parameter description of every cocyclic subring for $n\ge4$. The latter gives $2-2/(n-1)\le\alpha_n^{\cc}\le2$ for the global cocyclic convergence abscissa, and hence $\alpha_n^{\cc}\to2$. An exact quadratic family of quintic diagonal counts gives absolute convergence of the residual Dirichlet series for $\Rea s>19/13$. All asymptotics are obtained by elementary summation and absolutely convergent convolution.

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
papers.abstract: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.

papers.title: The Barker--Larman problem in dimension three A counterexample to the Barker--Larman problem in dimension three
papers.abstract: We construct an origin-symmetric convex body of revolution in \(\R^3\), with real-analytic boundary and positive principal curvatures, whose planar sections tangent to a concentric inner ball all have the same area. The body is nonspherical and has the same section data as a centered ball. The construction bifurcates from the unit ball at height \(1/\sqrt{3}\), where degree two is the only even Legendre resonance. We construct approximate solutions to arbitrary order and correct them by a Newton iteration on nested closed parameter sets. A finite-order reduction of the linearized section operator and measure estimates for its small divisors provide the inverse bounds needed for convergence.

papers.title: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
papers.abstract: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},\Sigma},U_n^\mathrm{\'et}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{\'et}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric \'etale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $\Sigma$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

papers.title: The Column-Diamond Resolution over Quadratic Monomial Rings
papers.abstract: We study infinite minimal free resolutions of modules $M = R/(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_m})$ over quadratic monomial rings $R = k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$. We introduce the Column-Diamond construction, a recursive diagrammatic procedure that builds an explicit free resolution of $M$ from columns and diamonds determined by the quadratic generators of $I$. We prove that this resolution is exact and minimal. As an application, the Betti numbers of $M$ are counted by valid words in a graph associated to $I$, which yields a combinatorial rational formula for the Poincar\'e series.

papers.title: The inductive Alperin–McKay condition for $G_2(q)$ and ${}^3D_4(q)$
papers.abstract: We verify the inductive Alperin–McKay condition for $G_2(q)$ ($q\geq3$) and ${}^3D_4(q)$ ($q\geq2$) at every odd prime.

papers.title: The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
papers.abstract: We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.

papers.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.title: The reciprocal cube sums of Lucas sequences of quadratic units are irrational
papers.abstract: Let $\eta>1$ be a unit of a real quadratic order and $U_n=(\eta^n-\bar\eta^n)/(\eta-\bar\eta)$ its Lucas sequence. We prove that $\sum_{n\ge1}U_n^{-3}$ is irrational. Equivalently, $\sum_{n\ge1}U_n(P,Q)^{-3}\notin\mathbb{Q}$ for the Lucas sequences with $Q=-1$, $P\ge1$, and with $Q=1$, $P\ge3$. In particular the sums of the reciprocal cubes of the Pell numbers and of the numbers $F_{kn}$, for every $k\ge1$, are irrational. The case of the Fibonacci numbers was treated in earlier work of the author; the proof here is the same Hankel-determinant construction, carried out for a general unit and for both signs of its norm. The constants of the argument do not depend on $\eta$ once they are measured in units of $\log\eta$. The whole argument is formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: The sum of the reciprocal cubes of the Fibonacci numbers is irrational
papers.abstract: We prove that $\zeta_F(3)=\sum_{n\ge1}F_n^{-3}$ is irrational, where $F_n$ are the Fibonacci numbers. To our knowledge the only odd value of the Fibonacci zeta function previously known to be irrational was $\zeta_F(1)$. The proof is a Hankel-determinant construction over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$, $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$, adapted from a recent unrefereed construction for the $q$-zeta value $\sum n^2/(p^n-1)$ at integers $p\ge2$. Four estimates are combined: a real decay of size $\exp(-\tfrac29K^3\log\varphi)$, a smallness $\exp(-K^3\log\varphi)$ at the Galois conjugate, which replaces the base-prime content gain of the integer case, local cyclotomic denominator bounds at the twisted roots of unity that occur, and nonvanishing by rational interpolation. The whole argument is formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Toric geometry of ReLU neural networks
papers.abstract: Given a continuous piecewise linear function $f:\mathbb{R}^{n_0} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a fixed architecture of feedforward ReLU neural networks, the exact function realization problem asks when a network of that architecture realizes $f$. In contrast, expressivity concerns characterizing all functions exactly realizable by a given architecture. To address these questions systematically, we establish a connection between toric geometry and ReLU neural networks, allowing tools from algebraic geometry to analyze the structures. Starting with an unbiased ReLU network with rational weights, we define the ReLU fan, the ReLU toric variety, and the ReLU Cartier divisor associated with the network. This work also relates the tropical and the toric geometry: the former captures combinatorial data of ReLU networks, while the latter recovers the underlying geometric structure. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the functions realizable by unbiased shallow ReLU networks with rational weights. The characterization is expressed in terms of intersection numbers of ReLU Cartier divisors with torus-invariant curves and leads to a decomposition of piecewise-linear functions into shallow and non-shallow components.

papers.title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
Towards a conformal field theory of critical percolation. I. The bulk stress tensor and Ward identities.
papers.abstract: We construct joint correlations of the bulk holomorphic stress tensor and the density field for critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, allowing any fixed finite numbers of insertions at separated points in the plane. Density correlations encode open-cluster connections; their two-point function is the renormalized probability that an open path joins two marked sites. Each stress insertion probes the directional response of these connections by closing and rotating a small ellipse and extracting the second angular component. To justify this construction, we extend Camia’s existence and conformal covariance results for density correlations from simply connected domains to the domains with finitely many analytic holes created by the ellipses, and prove uniform bounds for combining these correlations with the local ellipse responses. The main estimate controls the complete frontier record: the second angular coefficient has a comparable-scale defect of order (r/d)^(9/4), giving a Cauchy exponent 1/4 after quadratic normalization. The limits require no radius averaging, are distributions in the density coordinates, and are independent of the fixed ellipse shape parameters. They satisfy the conformal Ward identities with central charge zero and yield sequential stress-collision and contour identities.

papers.title: Transforming local positivity: from minimal valuations to irrational Seshadri constants
papers.abstract:
We explain how a valuative Nagata type statement proposed by Dumnicki, Harbourne, K\"uronya, Ro\'e and Szemberg on a polarised surface $(S, H)$ implies maximality (and hence often irrationality) of Seshadri constants on simple cyclic covers.
  As sample applications we show that very general degree two K3 surfaces and very general hypersurfaces in $\mathbb P^3$ of degree $6$, $8$ or $d\geq 10$ have irrational Seshadri constant at a very general point, unless $d$ is a square.

papers.title: Twisted Fourier-Mukai partners of genus 1 curves
papers.abstract: We study twisted derived equivalence between genus 1 curves over an arbitrarly perfect field.

papers.title: Undistillability of Werner states from three, four and five copies
papers.abstract: Whether every entangled state with a non-positive partial transpose (NPT) can be distilled is a long-standing open problem of entanglement theory. It reduces to the Werner states $\rho(d,\alpha)$, which for $d\ge3$ and $-1/2\le\alpha<-1/d$ are NPT but cannot be distilled from one copy; if one of them stays undistillable from every number of copies, NPT bound entanglement exists. We prove that for every $d\ge3$ the state $\rho(d,\alpha)$ is three-copy distillable if and only if $\alpha<-1/2$, the threshold known for one and two copies, so a third copy does not help. In every dimension we also prove four-copy undistillability for $\alpha\ge-79/160$ and five-copy undistillability for $\alpha\ge-9/20$, and improved bounds of order $1/k$ for $k\ge6$ copies. The proofs use a criterion of Costa Rico and computer-verified certificates for quartic moment relaxations that hold for all large dimensions at once; for many copies they combine the resulting inequalities with known partial-trace inequalities. Whether $-1/2$ remains the threshold from four copies on is open.

papers.title: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
papers.abstract: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators. Furthermore, using the universal TT-relations we derive exchange relations between spin-j Hamiltonians and the two non-local operators showing non-trivial symmetries for special boundary conditions, that they commute with all Hamiltonian densities. As another application of our universal TT-relations we propose universal T-system, Y-system and universal TQ-relations for $A_q$, and as a result, universal TQ for the q-Onsager algebra. For diagonal boundary conditions, we also obtain universal TT- and TQ-relations for a degenerate version of $A_q$ known as centrally extended augmented q-Onsager algebra. We finally discuss implications of our results for generalized Gibbs ensemble construction.

papers.title: Unramified multiplicity one spherical pairs
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $k$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$. We study the distinction between multiplicity one for unramified representations and multiplicity one for irreducible unitary representations. We prove that (G2, SL3) has the former property but not the latter. The unramified multiplicity one assertion uses spherical functions and the spherical Hecke module. For the failure of multiplicity one property, we use Weil representations and theta lifting to obtain an irreducible unitarizable representation with at least two independent SL3(k)-invariant linear forms.

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for the Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace problem
papers.abstract: The Schur–Siegel–Smyth trace constant $C_{86}$ is the lower limit of $\operatorname{tr}(\alpha)/\deg(\alpha)$ over totally positive algebraic integers $\alpha$. We prove $1.8022225<C_{86}<1.8070809$. For the upper bound we exhibit a measure on $[0,6]$ that satisfies the hypotheses of Smith's theorem on limits of distributions of conjugates, which we check with the help of $21$ integer polynomials. This improves the upper bounds $1.8216$ of Orloski and Talebizadeh Sardari and $1.8117251$ of Pinho. The lower bound comes from the method of Orloski, Talebizadeh Sardari and Smith with fifteen polynomials, three of them of degree $10$ found by McKee and Smyth. It is larger than the bound $1.80220$ reported by Giraudin, whose verification evaluates its bounds in floating-point arithmetic with fixed safety margins; ours encloses every rounding error. For each bound, two separately written programs check the certificate in ball arithmetic. Both bounds are also proved in Lean 4, the upper bound under the assumption of Smith's theorem, also in a version in which all checks on the certificates are carried out by Lean's kernel. We also give evidence that certificates of this kind cannot lower the upper bound much further without integer polynomials of high degree.

papers.title: Vector bundles on spin K\"ahler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
papers.abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin K\"ahler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.

papers.title: Vector Packing and Sharp Bounds for Matrices of Bounded Rank
papers.abstract: We prove a packing theorem in real and complex normed spaces. Given a possibly infinite family of vectors $(v_j)$ whose span has finite dimension $r\ge1$, let $M$ be the supremum of the norms of its finite linear combinations with coefficients of modulus at most one. If $M$ is finite, the family splits into $r$ nonempty sets, each with sum of norms at most $M$. The same partition works for every norm on the span, using that norm's value of $M$. We also determine exactly which finite lists of nonnegative numbers can be realized as the norms of a family of capacity one in some normed space of dimension at most $k$. We also obtain sharp rank-dependent bounds for products of the moduli of the entries on generalized diagonals and the permanent of the entrywise modulus, extending the known nonnegative-matrix bounds to real and complex matrices. The packing theorem also gives sharp support and entropy bounds for doubly stochastic matrices of bounded rank.

papers.title: Vieta invariants and Markoff–Hurwitz orbits
papers.abstract: We classify rational Vieta invariants for Guéritaud's family in characteristic zero, including every nonzero fiber. For each positive integer coefficient and each dimension residue class, we construct infinitely many Markoff–Hurwitz equations with infinitely many maxima shared by at least any prescribed number of distinct positive integer orbits.

papers.title: Wasserstein geometry of analytic cycle spaces
papers.abstract: We use optimal transport to define an intrinsic distance on connected components of the Barlet space of analytic cycles on a compact K\"ahler manifold, by associating to each cycle its normalized volume measure. We prove that any two cycles in the same connected component can be joined by a deformation of finite Wasserstein length, and that the resulting metric is complete and geodesic. On the locus of smooth reduced cycles at regular parameter points, Wasserstein lengths and energies coincide with those of the normalized Weil--Petersson metric. The construction thus gives a transport interpretation of Weil--Petersson geometry and extends beyond it to components containing no smooth reduced cycles.

papers.title: Weakly special varieties, Campana stacks, and Remarks on Orbifold Mordell
papers.abstract: We construct the first weakly special surfaces that are not Campana-special, including the complement of the plane curve $x^2y^3 = 1$ in $\mathbb{A}^2$. We prove that the set of $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}$-integral points on this surface is non-dense for every number field $K$ and finite set $S$ of finite places of $K$ if and only if Campana's Orbifold Mordell conjecture holds for $(\mathbb{G}_m, \tfrac{1}{2}[1])$. This basic example carries a natural $\mathbb{G}_m$-action, and the quotient stack is an Artin stack parametrizing points on a C-pair. This leads to the introduction of "Campana stacks", which encode morphisms of C-pairs in a manner analogous to the role of root stacks for integral points satisfying prescribed divisibility conditions.
